survey: A cartoon meteor/asteroid. Main body: one lumpy grey-brown rock seen at a three-quarter angle, facing the camera at lower left. It has one large crater, one medium crater on the right side, a small crater in the middle, a crater on the bottom edge and scattered pits. The rock has no supports or attachments, and that is correct for an object flying through space. The flame trail is three orange teardrop-shaped flames. They grow from the back and upper-right of the rock and stream up and to the right, opposite the direction of travel (toward the lower left), so the trail is consistent with the motion. Each flame tip ends in one or two small round sparks, a common cartoon way to show trailing embers. The flames sit flush against the rock with no gap, and none of them pass through the body. The craters are plausible impact shapes, and nothing is duplicated or mirrored where it should match.
